ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC$ is inscribed in $\odot O$, and $AB=AC$. Let $P$ be a point on the arc $\overset{\frown}{AC}$, and $\angle BAC=30^\circ$. If the radius of $\odot O$ is 6, find the length of the arc $\overset{\frown}{APC}$ (keep $\pi$ in the result).
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw the lines OA and OC.

$\because \angle ABC=75^\circ$,

$\therefore \angle AOC=2\angle ABC=2\times 75^\circ=150^\circ$,

$\therefore L_{\overset{\frown}{APC}} = \frac{150\pi R}{180}=\frac{5}{6}\pi \times 6=\boxed{5\pi}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, and triangle ABC is inscribed in the circle; A is above the circle, B is at the lower left, and C is at the lower right. Point P is located on the right-side arc of the circle from A to C, therefore arc APC represents the shorter arc AC passing through P. Reasoning: From the problem statement, AB=AC, so triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle, the vertex angle ∠BAC=30°, therefore the base angles ∠ABC=∠BCA=(180°-30°)/2=75°. The inscribed angle ∠ABC intercepts arc AC, so the corresponding central angle ∠AOC=2∠ABC=150°, that is, the measure of arc APC is 150°. The circle radius R=6, and the arc length is (150/360)·2π·6=5π.
